References and credits

Source: vignettes/articles/credits.Rmd
credits.Rmd

IRTistic is built on decades of psychometric research and on the work of the authors of many R packages. Its estimation code is written from scratch, but its methods, conventions and many of its design ideas come from the people listed below. If you use IRTistic in published work, please cite IRTistic and the methodological sources for the procedures you report.

citation("IRTistic")

Software that inspired and validates IRTistic

Methodological references, by feature

  • Birnbaum, A. (1968). Some latent trait models and their use in inferring an examinee’s ability. In F. M. Lord & M. R. Novick, Statistical theories of mental test scores (pp. 397-479). Addison-Wesley.
  • Barton, M. A., & Lord, F. M. (1981). An upper asymptote for the three-parameter logistic item-response model (ETS Research Report RR-81-20). Educational Testing Service.
  • Samejima, F. (1969). Estimation of latent ability using a response pattern of graded scores. Psychometrika Monograph Supplement, 34(4, Pt. 2), No. 17.
  • Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. Psychometrika, 43(4), 561-573.
  • Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47(2), 149-174.
  • Muraki, E. (1992). A generalized partial credit model: Application of an EM algorithm. Applied Psychological Measurement, 16(2), 159-176.
  • Bock, R. D., & Aitkin, M. (1981). Marginal maximum likelihood estimation of item parameters: Application of an EM algorithm. Psychometrika, 46(4), 443-459.
  • Warm, T. A. (1989). Weighted likelihood estimation of ability in item response theory. Psychometrika, 54(3), 427-450.

  • Wright, B. D., & Stone, M. H. (1979). Best test design. MESA Press.
  • Wright, B. D., & Masters, G. N. (1982). Rating scale analysis. MESA Press.

Graphics

The colour palette and chart conventions were chosen for legibility in print and for readers with colour-vision deficiency. Plots are built with ggplot2 (Wickham, 2016).
